              "title": "event-loop sentinel SIGKILLs an operator host whose main thread is in D-state (0 CPU, waiting on disk I/O) during host-wide I/O saturation, losing in-flight requests",
              "summary": "OBSERVATION (measured 2026-10-01 ~01:30-01:36Z, su-e445ff19): verify-tauri-headless rig for EAA P-014 c1 run 10 (/tmp/verify-tauri-headless.DKr0I7/tauri.log). Line ~905: '[event-loop-sentinel] main event loop STALLED { stalenessMs: 10008, mainThreadActivity: parked, mainThreadState: D, mainThreadCpuMsDuringStall: 0, ... }', then line 908 'main event loop WEDGED — SIGKILLing the host { stalenessMs: 24021, consecutiveStale: 3, mode: kill }', line 911 'operator dev server exited code=137 — restarting'. An in-flight owner MCP call (pot:create) got only the ':stream-open' SSE prime and then nothing, so the acceptance run failed at setup.\n\nHOST STATE AT THE SAME TIME: /proc/pressure/io some avg10=69.35 full avg10=58.66 (avg60 full 37.85); /proc/pressure/cpu some avg10=0.72. 90 processes in D state, 68 of them node-MainThread, 23 postgres, plus kworker flush-259:1. loadavg 237/204/173 on 128 cores (load is D-state waiters, not CPU). Dirty 2.4 GB. Two-sample /proc/*/io write_bytes over 5 s: top writer pid 1469618 'bash /tmp/pcv/verify-tauri-headless-source.XLpRbK --boot-only' (cgroup pc-0muocusjd1jdzfouuns, fleet nonp2p-feature-drain-sol61-xhigh-0930 member, PAPERCUSP_SID su-f4fac3be) 2463.8 MB/5s incl. reaped children; next claude -p 265 MB, psu-launchers ~110-130 MB each.\n\nWHY IT IS A DEFECT: a D-state main thread with zero CPU during the stall is blocked in the kernel on I/O; SIGKILL cannot shorten that wait, it drops every in-flight request, and the restart adds boot I/O to the same saturated disk. The sentinel already records mainThreadState and mainThreadCpuMsDuringStall but still kills. [inferred] The same path may explain repeated :3070/:3170 restarts that drop MCP clients (EI-24690003269578622); not checked.\n\nSUGGESTED FIX: when the stall is D-state with ~0 main-thread CPU and host PSI io full is high, do not kill: log, record, and re-evaluate (or kill only after a much longer bound); separately, admission-control heavy verify-tauri-headless boots on disk I/O (they write GBs each) the way pc-heavy gates CPU.\n\nⓘ Possible STALE RUNTIME, not an open defect: `packages/operator-core/lib` (240 newer commits, tip `244f7d127cc8290334d0e30f3633ffe39838056f`) have commits newer than the running build (`29bf735091`) in `staging`.               "title": "mutation-probe.sh with a with-test-pg --isolated-runtime guard fails as harness-error unless the caller exports PAPERCUSP_TEST_RUNS_DB_URL",
              "summary": "Observed 2026-10-11 02:58Z (su-6baa8, WI-10008042 P-002 clean re-proof). Command, run from a lint:as-committed materialized clone at 2f78f6b3b0: scripts/mutation-probe.sh --file packages/operator-core/lib/harness/improvements/agent-review.ts --mutate ... --test 'PROBE_SUBJECT={} node scripts/with-test-pg.mjs --isolated-runtime -- env PAPERCUSP_LINT_AS_COMMITTED_CLONE=1 npm run test:file -- .../agent-review-plan-route.integration.test.ts' --expect caught --relocation overlay. Result: 'MUTATION_PROBE_RESULT verdict=harness-error baseline_exit=1 guard_exit=-1'. The cause is one log line: '[with-test-pg] evidence preflight failed: PAPERCUSP_TEST_RUNS_DB_URL is required for durable isolated test receipts' (scripts/with-test-pg.mjs ~L58). That preflight fires whenever PAPERCUSP_TEST_RUN_RECEIPT_FILE or PC_EXECUTED_SOURCE_MAP_RESULT is set, and mutation-probe sets one of them. A capability:bash shell does not export PAPERCUSP_TEST_RUNS_DB_URL, and the same command worked for su-055e916b on 2026-10-10. The verdict only says harness-error. Workaround: export PAPERCUSP_TEST_RUNS_DB_URL to the shared ledger (the same default as scripts/run-operator-e2e-isolated.sh). Suggested fix: mutation-probe.sh should preflight this before the baseline when --test runs 'with-test-pg --isolated-runtime' and name the env var in its refusal. Alternatively, the 'Proving a guard is falsifiable' docs should state the requirement. Evidence: .papercusp/scratch/6baa8-p002-probes/signed-auth-clean.log (first run, overwritten by the rerun; the line is quoted above).\n\nⓘ Possible STALE RUNTIME, not an open defect: `scripts/mutation-probe.sh` (64 newer commits, tip `312d1a112ad53ab1d39dfd1990f9b47d8b5047b1`), `scripts/with-test-pg.mjs` (25 newer commits, tip `714072d2b207a9b9e9e85e53daa2ba2fa942597d`) have commits newer than the running build (`d740fc3802`) in `staging`.             "checkpoint": "## Did\nRoot cause: the fetch guard in packages/operator-core/lib/harness/git-sync/git-fetch-headroom.ts correctly refuses Git fetches when free bytes are at or below criticalWriteHeadroomBytes. The measured root filesystem is 2,013,991,550,976 bytes total, so the reported 40,279,831,019-byte reserve matches the source rule. `df` on the exact cart-drawer/chat-protocol object-store paths returned 33,897,168,896 bytes free on the latest sample (~6.38 GB below reserve). Earlier samples were 38.68 GB, 37.80 GB, and 43.65 GB. A bounded read-only top-level `du` showed /home/marsh-office/storewolf-central-server at 31,995,330,560 bytes, `.papercusp-relocated-builds` at 8,191,950,848, and `snap` at 4,250,251,264. The largest path is a separate Git checkout with many tracked modifications.\n\n## Left\nStill open: identify a policy-safe reclaim source or await root headroom recovery, then verify the affected install's own scheduled sync and fetch path. The responsible root-pressure work item WI-6554700010008795 remains wip on su-0dd6b9aa, but targeted presence returned no live session, its named rootdu artifact was absent, and there was no pickup confirmation after one required wake. The fleet leader has been sent both the capacity deficit and the stale root-item ownership evidence. I did not delete or prune anything. /mnt/data is a separate filesystem at 10,392,014,848 bytes free and is not the backing filesystem for these Git object stores. Another reported fact — three sidestage sync commits through 05:56Z and the peer's passing committed R3 suite — only proves partial progress; it does not establish current fetch admission while root is below reserve.\n\n## Key insight\nThe reserve breach is the measured proximate cause of the recorded fetch refusal; the producer intentionally keeps this guard. Root-space occupant ownership and a safe reclaim target are not established. The largest measured directory is not a safe cleanup target because the checkout has numerous tracked modifications.\n\n## Next action\nAfter an authorized root-space recovery, remeasure `df -B1` on the exact object-store paths and verify the sidestage routine's scheduled fetch/commit progress in its own install scope. If the reserve remains breached, get a live admitted owner for WI-6554700010008795 or another policy-approved reclaim source; do not retry cross-hive git-sync:run or delete the modified storewolf checkout.\n\n## Checks\n_✓ = VERIFIED (evidence attached) · ⚠ = CONTESTED (evidence contradicts verification; re-check now) · ? = PREDICTED (observed context may be attached) — run the re-check before relying on it · [scope: …] = ALL the probe observed; a claim quantified beyond it is NOT verified by it_\n- ? [#root-pressure-owner-presence] Targeted hive presence currently returns no row for the old holder of WI-6554700010008795. — re-check: coord:presence { owner: 'su-0dd6b9aa-3d59-4727-991e-377d05bc2459', scope: 'hive' } (since 2026-10-12T06:53:37.962Z)\n- ?               "title": "CLAUDE.md prescribes work_items:set_blocker { defaultIfUnanswered, decideBy } but the tool schema has neither field",
              "summary": "Observed 2026-10-26 ~20:47Z (su-96b7fe62). The project guide (CLAUDE.md, section 'A blocker is work') says: 'A reversible judgment call you could make yourself is not an owner wall — park it. Call work_items:set_blocker { id, kind:\"product-decision\", ref, defaultIfUnanswered, decideBy }: it opens a peer review of your default ... silence by the deadline means proceed.' tools:find for work_items:set_blocker (registry projected-tool-registry-v1:2683a730a1ee2f6f) returns argSchema top-level keys id, kind, capability, ref, summary, evidence, nextVerb, clear, harness, items, with no defaultIfUnanswered and no decideBy. An agent following the guide either gets an invalid_args refusal or (if extra keys are stripped) a product-decision blocker with no default and no deadline, so silence never means proceed.               "summary": "Observed 2026-10-28: a Papercusp local-sync ran from 17:30:14Z through at least 18:28:33Z (~58m), then last_synced_at advanced to 18:28:33Z.               "checkpointProseSnapshot": "## Did\nImplemented requested-path reconciliation and synthetic Vitest collection failures in `testing/run.ts`; added mixed-report and zero-suite regressions. Coordinated with su-71117: EI-27284386875003015's per-router-group source identity and timeout-recovery custody is a separate change on overlapping files. Exact staging test row 22986806 / run group d3dde834-3493-468e-8da7-d5ff11f07925 passes both target cases (2 passed, 0 failed, 116 skipped by name filter) at commit 752949c27dde8d3e571678065c959c4233d5573d; durable row also names both case titles. Earlier focused row 22985380 passed five selected cases.\n\n## Left\nNo code edits remain for EI-27289605425626062. Release lock a19aac92-b204-4647-9e7e-b31b93d8fe56, then close with rootCauseVerification and the durable 2/2 case evidence. No residue identified.\n\n## Key insight\nThe failure originates in `run.ts` report reconciliation: Vitest may omit a requested test file when collection fails, while sibling or empty JSON output still exists. Reconciliation now compares requested Vitest paths to reported `byFile` entries, synthesizes per-file failures, and retains a bounded redacted router diagnostic.\n\n## Next action\nClose EI-27289605425626062 after releasing its two file locks; continue the already-held EI-27156491392451841 item next."

              "kind": "bug",

              "harness": "papercusp",
              "title": "Docker container create and start hang in overlay filesystem unmount/writeback on staging host",
              "summary": "Measured 2026-09-26 22:45-22:53 EDT on the canonical staging host. A stock `docker run --rm --pull=never --network none ubuntu:24.04 /bin/sh -c echo` timed out with no output at both 90s and 30s; `docker start` of a created container timed out at 30s. Docker status reads stayed responsive. Dockerd SIGUSR1 dump `/var/run/docker/goroutine-stacks-2026-09-26T224713-0400.log` shows two create handlers in overlay2.Driver.Put -> unix.Unmount for >2m. Kernel task stacks and hung-task reports at 22:19 and 22:30 show ovl_sync_fs -> sync_inodes_sb / wb_wait_for_completion. This prevents the PUI release-acceptance stock Linux smoke and leaves exact-r12 scorecard checks unmeasured (EI-24373052706582252). A reversible vm.dirty_background_bytes=512MiB / vm.dirty_bytes=2GiB experiment reduced Dirty 8GB to 2GB but a new docker run still timed out; original ratios were restored. High Dirty is therefore not established as the cause. Diagnose what is holding overlay unmount/writeback, fix it durably, and add an automated Docker create/start health guard that catches this before acceptance checks.",

              "kind": "bug",
              "family": "issue",
              "harness": "papercusp",
              "title": "release-fixer blueprint spawns intermittently return HTTP 200 with an empty turn (infra_loss, no thread/turn started) — most recent occurrence ran on Claude Sonnet 4.5, not codex",
              "summary": "Found while investigating WI-2141080 (codex-gateway routing for blueprint fixers). Queried `harness_shared.spawned_agents` (workspace_id='papercusp-workspace', harness_slug='papercusp') for recent release-fixer spawns and found a failure signature DISTINCT from the codex-usage-limit story WI-2141080 was filed around:\n\nTwo spawns in the last ~24h carry `error_message` starting `infra_loss: papercusp/release-fixer returned HTTP 200 but the agent produced no turn (ok=false, exitCode=1, timedOut=false, outLen=0; rawStdoutTail=...)`:\n- `s-1788269784190-a44a00e7` — 2026-09-01 13:36:24Z, duration 31258ms, exit_code 1, pid 4168572\n- `s-1788347848159-08ee8702` — 2026-09-02 11:17:28Z, duration 80218ms, exit_code 1, pid 315841\n\nNeither shows a usage-limit message, and neither reached `thread.started`/`turn.started` per the error text — the HTTP call to `/invoke` returned 200 but the spawned agent produced zero output. The most recent one's `rawStdoutTail` contains a live models-list response headed by `\"id\":\"claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929\"` — i.e. this spawn was running on a CLAUDE backend, not codex/gpt, and still died empty. So this is NOT the codex-CLI-credential-routing issue WI-2141080 tracks; it reproduces independent of backend/provider.\n\nOnly 2 occurrences found in a 24h window, both release-fixer (no other child_role matched `error_message ILIKE '%infra_loss%'` in the same window) — could be role-specific (its brief/prompt size, a tool-call shape it uses) or just the only role that spawned enough times to surface it. Root cause not yet investigated: worth checking the orchestrator's /invoke handler for what \"HTTP 200 + ok:false + exitCode 1 + outLen 0\" actually means (a crash before the first turn callback fires? a caught-and-swallowed exception?) and whether it correlates with anything about the release-fixer blueprint/brief specifically.\n\nCURRENT IMPACT: this is the failure mode on the single MOST RECENT release-fixer attempt (2026-09-02 11:17:28Z) — i.e. right now, independent of the codex-account-pool exhaustion tracked on WI-2141080, this is what's actually stopping the gate from self-healing via release-fixer.\n\nQuery used:\n```sql\nSELECT spawn_id, started_at, duration_ms, exit_code, pid, error_message\nFROM harness_shared.spawned_agents\nWHERE workspace_id='papercusp-workspace' AND harness_slug='papercusp'\n  AND error_message ILIKE '%infra_loss%' AND started_at > now() - interval '24 hours'\nORDER BY started_at DESC;\n```",

              "title": "Admission-disposition event blockers make their own receipt requests ineligible",
              "summary": "A direct DRAIN blocker affects EI-26706336823221530 and EI-26709554968565192. Both items have active external blocker `harness:papercusp:admission-disposition`; generation 3 requires canonical admission-review receipts for those same item/request IDs. In staging, `work_items:review-admission` refused the current custodian request with `review subject has a terminal, human, policy, mixed or unproven park/dependency`. Source `admissionReviewCustodyEligible` permits only the item's own admission-review alert blocker, so the harness gate itself prevents replacing requests signed by ended callers. The gate consequently cannot receive the receipts it requires.               "title": "Stale active-inference recovery marker can suppress loop stall detection after a cold wake",
              "summary": "Direct DRAIN blocker: at 2026-11-02T12:46Z, live loop:status showed lastFiredAt=2026-11-02T11:35:15.573Z, executionRecovery.status=running/reason=active-inference with observedAt=1793619506595 (~11:38Z) and nextProbeAt=1793619536595 (~11:38Z), lastLoopTurnAt=null, rewakeGuaranteed=false/last-fire-no-loop-turn, yet turnsStalled=false. Source cause: packages/operator-core/lib/harness/routines/loop.ts treats any running active-inference marker with observedAt >= lastFiredAt as current, without a freshness bound. packages/operator-core/lib/harness/routines/loop-execution-recovery.ts updates metadata for protect only when status/reason/generation/attempts/verifiedSuccessorFireAt change, omitting observedAt and nextProbeAt, so repeated identical active-inference observations can remain stale. Existing loop.test.ts covers a marker older than lastFiredAt, not a stale marker that is still newer than that fire. Existing done EI-26069482705773450 covers a different delivery-path fix; linked as related context. Recurrence blocks safe DRAIN continuation; fix the source freshness/write predicate and add a conventional regression test. No source edit or test run yet.",

            "checkpoint": "## Did\nThe exact historical DBOS workflow record has status ERROR; operation 2 (system:work-item-admission-promoter) records CONNECT_TIMEOUT and no output. Current source order is lock-client reserve/advisory lock, followed by admissionPromoterPass, whose first deps.sql call is completedOrdinaryResult. The bounded DBOS query for promoter operations created since 00:00Z returned four rows and all four have status SUCCESS, including runs at 00:35Z and 01:37Z. The original error predates the reserve-phase annotation and contains no phase/callsite marker.\n\n## Left\nThe actual historical client/callsite and TCP cause remain unknown. The reserve marker is future diagnostic, not a durable root-cause fix. A consult found no qualified responder, and the two candidate owners had no indexed transcripts.
